$$ \det \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix} = (5)(4) - (1)(2) = 20 - 2 = 18 $$
Thus, the area is:
$$ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} | 18 | = 9 $$

**Alternative Method: Coordinate Geometry (Shoelace Formula)**
Let the vertices be $(0,0)$, $(5,1)$, and $(2,4)$.
$$ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} | x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2) | $$
Substitute the coordinates:
$$ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} | 0(1 - 4) + 5(4 - 0) + 2(0 - 1) | $$
$$ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} | 0 + 20 - 2 | $$
$$ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} | 18 | $$
$$ \text{Area} = 9 $$

Both methods yield the same result.

\boxed{9}
